0.name: Amritmahal
0.overview: Amritmahal is a hardy draught breed from Karnataka, valued for its compact muscular build, stamina and ability to work under relatively low-input conditions. It is primarily associated with farm and transport work rather than high milk production.

top_5_characteristics.title: Build
top_5_characteristics.description: Medium-to-large, compact and muscular, suited to sustained work.

top_5_characteristics.title: Coat
top_5_characteristics.description: Usually grey, ranging from white to very dark grey or almost black.

top_5_characteristics.title: Horns
top_5_characteristics.description: Long horns emerge close together, sweep backward/upward, then turn inward.

top_5_characteristics.title: Work ability
top_5_characteristics.description: Strong draught capacity with good stamina for farm and transport work.

top_5_characteristics.title: Adaptation
top_5_characteristics.description: Well adapted to Karnataka conditions and relatively low-input management.

care_guide.feeding: Base the ration on good-quality roughage and local green fodder; add concentrate/mineral support when the animal is doing sustained draught work. Keep feed changes gradual.
care_guide.housing: Provide a dry, shaded, well-ventilated shelter with a non-slip floor and clean bedding. Protect from prolonged rain or extreme heat according to the home climate. Prioritize shade, airflow and access to cool drinking water during heat waves.
care_guide.grazing_or_exercise: Allow regular grazing or controlled exercise. For working animals, schedule water, rest and cooling breaks and avoid the hottest part of the day.
care_guide.healthcare: Follow the local veterinary vaccination schedule, routine deworming and parasite control. Check hooves/feet regularly because workload and terrain increase wear.
care_guide.breeding_or_milking: Select healthy animals from sound working lines. Avoid breeding animals with structural limb or hoof problems; pregnancy and postpartum care should be supervised locally.
care_guide.handling_note: Use calm, low-stress handling and provide secure fencing and clean water points.

1.name: Ayrshire
1.overview: Ayrshire is a Scottish dairy breed included in this classifier as an exotic cattle class. It is recognized for efficient milk production, strong dairy conformation and adaptability to grazing-based systems, although management in India should consider local climate and heat stress.

top_5_characteristics.title: Origin
top_5_characteristics.description: A Scottish dairy breed; it is an exotic class in relation to Indian indigenous breeds.

top_5_characteristics.title: Coat
top_5_characteristics.description: Typically red or brown with white markings, often sharply patterned.

top_5_characteristics.title: Dairy type
top_5_characteristics.description: Selected primarily for milk production and efficient grazing.

top_5_characteristics.title: Udder
top_5_characteristics.description: Generally well-developed dairy conformation with balanced quarters.

top_5_characteristics.title: Climate need
top_5_characteristics.description: Performs best with heat-stress control in hot Indian climates.

care_guide.feeding: Provide a balanced ration built around quality green fodder, dry roughage, clean water and an appropriate mineral mixture. Increase energy/protein supply according to milk yield and stage of lactation.
care_guide.housing: Use a clean, dry, well-ventilated shed with shade and adequate drainage. Keep milking and resting areas hygienic.
care_guide.grazing_or_exercise: Provide daily movement or grazing appropriate to body condition and climate. Reduce heat load with shade, airflow and frequent access to water in hot weather.
care_guide.healthcare: Follow the local vaccination and deworming plan; maintain tick/parasite control and monitor appetite, manure, body condition, udder health and lameness. In hot Indian conditions, heat-stress monitoring is especially important because this is a temperate dairy breed.
care_guide.breeding_or_milking: Use clean milking practices and consistent milking times. Breed only when the animal is in suitable body condition; use a veterinarian/technician for fertility problems.
care_guide.handling_note: Use calm, low-stress handling and provide secure fencing and clean water points.

1.dataset_note: Ayrshire is not an indigenous Indian breed; it originated in Scotland and is included because it is one of the labels in the supplied classifier dataset.

48.name: siri
48.overview: Siri is a hill cattle breed from the eastern Himalayan region, especially associated with Sikkim and neighbouring areas. It is adapted to cool, wet and mountainous terrain and is valued for hardiness, mobility and utility in low-input farming systems.
